decision_authority: User supplied current Production screenshots on 2026-09-19 showing Spartacus reverted again to polity/relation unknown. Direct Production API read-back confirmed Activity 6c7e0f1c-d843-4b8a-a436-fad247840b31 is again polity_id=null and relation_type_id=null with the superseded 2026-08-23 opponent-context note. Root cause is now identified in code: every Correction Apply replays db/migrations/20260823_person_polity_community_reviewed_corrections.sql through applyCorrectionMigrations, and that historical migration deterministically rewrites this exact surviving Spartacus Activity from Roman Republic/opposes back to null/null. This repair is paired with the replay-safety code fix so future unrelated corrections cannot reintroduce the regression.

evidence.current_production_readback: 2026-09-19 direct /api/atlas-person-read list and detail both return polity=null, relation=null, interval 73-71 BCE, role Rebel leader, and the superseded note 'Roman Republic is opponent context, not Spartacus's primary polity.'
evidence.root_cause: server/atlas-correction-apply-handler.js calls applyCorrectionMigrations before every apply. server/atlas-correction-migrations.js previously replayed the full POST_STAGE2_MIGRATION_PATHS, including the identity-bound 20260823 data migration. That migration contains an exact Spartacus block which converts Roman Republic/opposes to null/null. Because Spartacus retained the same Activity UUID while other reviewed resistance cases were later replaced/split, Spartacus uniquely kept getting reverted by unrelated later Correction Apply runs.
evidence.rationale: The modeled Activity is the Third Servile War against the Roman Republic. ATLAS relation semantics represent that explicit counterparty as Roman Republic / opposes; this does not imply allegiance, service, or membership.

after.reviewed_notes: Spartacus led the major slave revolt against the Roman Republic traditionally called the Third Servile War from 73 to 71 BCE. ATLAS binds this Activity to the Roman Republic with relation opposes because the polity is the historically explicit opponent of the rebellion; this binding does not imply allegiance, service, or membership.
